scope: Q4.4 synthetic public-API workflow example and integration fixture only; no clinical policy, multi-resource atomic operation, portable checkpoint/restore, release, or full ED workflow claim.

basis.plan: conductor/tracks/des_queue_preemption_20260925/plan.md Q4.4 and Q4 exit same-runtime event-boundary parity
basis.api: libs/kairos/crates/kairo-ecs-des/src/flow.rs public FlowRuntime, AcquireBuilder, typed create_work context, request/resource inspection, release, run_for/step

proposed_paths.shared_execution: Example owns pub fn run(mode: RunMode) -> Result<WorkflowOutput, FlowError>; integration test imports the same example source with #[path = "../examples/flow_staff_bed_cleaning.rs"] mod scenario and calls run(Continuous) and run(PausedAtBoundaries). The example main calls run(Continuous), so the user-facing runnable sample and assertions exercise identical setup, dispatch loop, caller actions, record projection, and conservation checks.

requests.normal_staff_request: normal staff claim, priority 10, preemptible Suspend
requests.urgent_staff_request: urgent staff claim, priority 2, can_preempt true
requests.patient_b_bed_request: manual Bed-A claim submitted during cleaning, priority 10

fixture_entities_and_exact_aliases.identity_rule: These are deterministic fixture aliases mapped to public generational IDs returned by FlowRuntime; do not hard-code raw ECS EntityId values or attach components directly. Keep care-related labels only in fixture data, not in Kairos policy.

typed_context: Register one concrete Rust FixtureContext type with case_id, actor_label, task_label, and phase enum. Attach it to normal and urgent staff work (and cleaning work if useful). On normal-work Suspend and Resume assert work_context::<FixtureContext>() retains the same case/task identity and expected phase; no clone/serialization/codec is used or implied.

actions: Submit normal_staff_request on staff_resource for Staff-A, timed_work normal_staff_work, priority 10, preemptible Suspend; dispatch its grant first.
Only after the staff grant boundary, submit patient_a_bed_request on Bed-A for Patient-A as a separate manual one-resource claim; dispatch Bed-A grant and retain its LeaseId.
Assert Bed-A active=1/available=0 and Staff-A-duty active=1/available=0. The order explicitly stages staff then bed; there is no combined acquisition.
exact_timeline_ticks.expected: Normal staff Granted, then Patient-A Bed-A Granted; one active lease per capacity-one resource.

actions: Submit urgent_staff_request for Staff-A on staff_resource with timed_work urgent_staff_work, priority 2 and can_preempt=true.
exact_timeline_ticks.expected: Normal work Preempted with Suspend and 5 ticks remaining; urgent work Granted. Staff active count remains 1.

actions: Urgent work completes and normal work resumes with the original typed context and 5 ticks remaining.
Submit cleaning_request on the separate cleaning_resource for Cleaner-A with timed_work cleaning_work, duration 2. Keep Patient-A's manual Bed-A LeaseId active.
exact_timeline_ticks.expected: Urgent Completed; normal Resumed; Cleaner-A cleaning Granted; Bed-A remains active=1/available=0. No bed+cleaner atomic request.

actions: Submit patient_b_bed_request for Patient-B against Bed-A while Patient-A's lease is still held and cleaning is in progress.
exact_timeline_ticks.expected: Patient-B is Queued; Bed-A active=1/available=0; Patient-B is not Granted. Queue contains exactly patient_b_bed_request.

actions: Cleaning work completes. At that completion boundary, caller explicitly releases Patient-A's saved manual Bed-A lease at runtime.now(). Process the resulting release/arbitration event; capture Patient-B's grant. Then explicitly release Patient-B's manual lease at the same runtime time and process the release event to drain allocations.
exact_timeline_ticks.expected: Bed-A never has available capacity before Patient-A release. Patient-B Granted only after the release event at tick 7, then Released; final Bed-A active=0/available=1 and queue empty.

actions: Normal staff work completes after resuming its 5 remaining ticks; collect the final state and record output.
exact_timeline_ticks.expected: Normal work Completed once; Staff-A-duty active=0/available=1; all resources have zero active allocations and empty queues.

shared_run_output_contract.output: WorkflowOutput contains canonical named event tuples (tick, alias, transition, ordinal, queue_len, active_count, capacity, progress projection), per-boundary resource snapshots, final request/work states, and final typed context values. It does not expose raw ECS attachment dumps.
shared_run_output_contract.continuous: Drains the scheduled scenario while applying the documented caller actions exactly at t0 staff grant, t7 cleaner completion, and t7 Patient-B grant.
shared_run_output_contract.paused: Uses FlowRuntime::run_for/step to stop before/after selected event boundaries (urgent eviction/grant, t6 queued Patient-B, t7 cleaning completion/grant); continues those exact live FlowRuntime instances and applies the same caller actions at the same boundaries. It never reconstructs state from a snapshot.
shared_run_output_contract.parity: Integration test compares Continuous and PausedAtBoundaries WorkflowOutput exactly after mapping generational IDs to stable fixture aliases. Require equal timeline, lifecycle ordering/ordinals, resource snapshots, progress, terminal states, typed context, and final drained allocations. This is same-process same-runtime pause/continue only, not portable checkpoint or cross-process replay.

must_hold_invariants: At every inspected event boundary and after each explicit caller action, for each resource active_count <= capacity and available + active_count = capacity.
Bed-A occupancy starts only after Staff-A grant (separate staged claims), remains active through the entire cleaning interval [t5,t7], and Patient-B queues at t6 without grant.
At t7, the ordered causal sequence is cleaning Completed, Patient-A bed Released, Patient-B bed Granted, then Patient-B bed Released; no temporary available-bed gap permits an earlier grant.
Staff interruption uses only one staff unit; normal remaining duration is 5 at Suspend and is preserved at Resume; urgent work duration is 2; normal terminal completion is t10.
Every work/request uses at most one resource per request; no atomic multi-resource grant, implicit rollback, or clinical eligibility policy is included.
All times/durations are integer ticks; no RNG, wall clock, external input, or empirical parameter claim.
acceptance_limits: This is Q4.4 example plus integration evidence; Q4.5 remains the separate phase review.
The example is a synthetic staged resource workflow, not a complete ED workflow, calibrated model, release qualification, stable API approval, or portable checkpoint demonstration.
staff_leaf_scope: Create shared example runner staff-only phase with identical typed context, priorities, interruption/resume timeline0/3/5/10; tests first; bed extension is separate next leaf
bed_leaf_scope: Extend shared runner after accepted staff leaf with staged bed0, cleaning5-7, waiter6, releases7; tests first
raw_id_parity: Compare raw LifecycleRecord vectors as well as projected aliases between deterministic equivalent setup runs; do not discard event IDs/ordinals or snapshots for same-runtime parity.
cleaning_orchestration_boundary: Cleaning is an independent synthetic work resource. The caller retains manualBed-A lease until it observes cleaningCompleted; no automatic runtimecoupling between resources is implied.
context_lifetime: CurrentFlow retains typedcontext after timed completion; assert unchangedcontext atSuspend,Resume,andterminal. Onlydespawnremovesit; no portability claim.
